subject: P04
required_fixes: R1 — Reset does not fence API Client transfers and their protected-storage writes. workbench_domain.rs:835-856 releases the workbench lane before awaiting Send/Apply work. Sending::clear (send.rs:135-142) cancels active transfers and clears in-memory jars/history, but authority.rs:3056-3082 waits only for credential/learner/offline writers and the document lane before purging the Keychain namespace and API Client folder. A transfer already outside that lane still unconditionally calls store_history and may store its retained dirty cookie jar after cancellation (send.rs:1237-1263); pre-send preparation can also reach BodyWriter::create after the purge. profile.rs:140-147/:198-213 creates a missing profile key and writes private files, and history.rs:150-152 creates the response directory. A late worker can therefore recreate private storage and its key after a successful reset, including restoring persistent cookies held by its old jar. The current document reset test runs after work is settled, and the execution suite contains no reset-during-transfer case. Acceptance: make reset retire and synchronize all admitted workbench transfers, blocking preparation and history/body/cookie persistence before declaring the purge complete; late workers must neither recreate keys/files nor republish retired state. Add deterministic production-interface fixtures holding a transfer around preparation/persistence and one carrying a dirty persistent cookie, reset, release the workers, and verify after all completions and restart that the private folder/key/history/cookies remain removed, operator collection bytes remain unchanged, and nothing is replayed.
optional_suggestions: Generate phase packets with the previous phase's verified completion commit as their diff base. This packet uses the latest C15 commit e9df1db and its diff contains only new P04 evidence. For this review, the cumulative source scope was reconstructed independently from P03 commit bbbad4390ccb39aa906d88fa2b9440848b437675; its 426 reviewed source entries and modes match the retained P03 inventory. Including that cumulative diff directly would make future phase reviews easier to reproduce.
limitations: Read-only cumulative review: no application source was changed, no builds/tests or endpoints were launched, and no credentials were accessed. R1 is established by tracing production concurrency, cancellation and storage paths; the proposed deterministic race fixtures were not executed by this reviewer.
